props.title: Noise That Moves

B24.capture_spec: E1 (reused; DONE by script, 2026-10-13): two frames recorded in the same scratch project for the Textures and Color film and shown here because they show the same thing (the resource itself, not the slot's label, so the other film's shader does not show): `_godot-shaders-series/editor-capture/png/1920x1080/textures-and-color/textures-and-color_E1-3a_NoiseTexture2D-width-height-noise-FastNoiseLite.png` (the NoiseTexture2D view: Width, Height, Generate Mipmaps, Noise = FastNoiseLite, Color Ramp, Seamless, Invert, In 3D Space, As Normal Map, Normalize; NO preview) and `textures-and-color_E1-3b_inside-FastNoiseLite-preview-clouds.png` (the FastNoiseLite view: the grey clouds preview with a 3D button, Noise Type Simplex Smooth, Seed 0, Frequency 0.01, Offset, Fractal, Domain Warp). Both also exist as native 3456x1944 twins in png/3456x1944/textures-and-color/: crop those, x 1275 to 1915, y 195 to 555 in 1920 coordinates (times 1.8 for native). Cross-dissolve at 0.84; the ring boxes are fractions of that crop. (This film's own scene with a `noise` slot was never recorded: the frames above show the same two views.) No pointer: label 'scripted editor session'.
B24.visual_intent: Act title 'Noise That Moves' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left with the sampler line highlighted twice, each time with its definition label (noise, then texture). At right two real stills of Godot's Inspector from a scripted editor session, one after the other: first the NoiseTexture2D itself (Width 512 px, Height 512 px, its Noise slot holding a FastNoiseLite, a Seamless row; this view has no preview), with a terracotta ring on the NoiseTexture2D header and then on the Noise slot; then the FastNoiseLite itself, where the grey clouds preview appears, with the ring on the preview.
B24.motion_claim: The ring lands on the NoiseTexture2D, then on its Noise slot, then on the cloud preview of the generator, as the voice names them.

show.event: sampler line + 'noise' definition; the NoiseTexture2D view

B24.runner_up: ShaderLab render of the noise texture as teal alpha (labelled)
B24.why: The real Inspector is the thing the sentence names (SHOW-THE-THING), and the two views are the honest order: the texture holds a generator, the generator shows the clouds; the Lab render of the same texture does not show an editor.

cues.label: sampler2D: the type of a texture a shader reads
texture(noise, UV): a texture read at this address

B25.capture_spec: C11: scene script (`--scene`; the Lab only binds a plain image): NoiseTexture2D with FastNoiseLite defaults, 512 x 512, seamless on, bound to the 'noise' uniform of lab-shaders/10-noise-cloud.gdshader on the square target; still PNG 3840 x 2160, Forward+. Node setup as in evidence/planning-checks/noise_check.gd (make_noise, make_rect).
B25.visual_intent: Code card at left (the noise-cloud shader); at right the real render: the teal disc turned to cloud, bright patches where the noise is high and see-through patches where it is low.
B25.motion_claim: The three lines light up in turn while the clouds sit in the disc.

show.event: COLOR line: noise into the alpha

B25.why: The cloud is the real result of the lookup, next to the line that does it.

cues.label: TIME: seconds on one clock shared by the whole game

B26.capture_spec: C12: scene script as C11 (NoiseTexture2D seamless on) with lab-shaders/11-noise-scroll.gdshader; 12 s, 30 fps, Forward+, `--time-origin 0` so TIME is 0 at the first frame (no scripted input). Verified: a 3.0 s clock step moves the shader's TIME by 3.01 s and the pattern by 0.3 of the width, i.e. 0.1 per second (noise_check Z); the natural clock matched the engine's ticks in an earlier run (run-0 transcription, item 7).
B26.visual_intent: Code card at left (the scroll shader: the lookup now adds TIME times a tenth to the address); at right the real render: the clouds drift steadily sideways inside the disc. The TIME definition is on screen.
B26.motion_claim: The clouds drift while the lookup line is highlighted.
B26.why: A live render of the drift is the claim; the direction detail comes next.

B27.visual_intent: A long strip of noise bars (grey tones) with a terracotta window frame laid over it, the picture seen through the frame shown above. The frame slides right along the strip while the pattern seen through it shifts left. Labels 'lookup moves right' and 'picture moves left'; a readout '+0.125 → 32 px left' with the small grey credit 'Apple M4 Pro · Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+'.
B27.motion_claim: The frame slides right and the pattern inside it slides left.

show.event: strip, frame and the view through it
frame slides right; view shifts left

B27.why: A window sliding over a fixed strip is the exact reason the picture appears to move the other way.

B28.capture_spec: C13: scene script as C11 with lab-shaders/12-noise-no-repeat.gdshader; 12 s, 30 fps, Forward+, `--time-origin 0`. Verified: a raw greyscale check with lookups past 1.0 has row standard deviation 0.0 in the clamped half (identical along every row) and 0.1485 with repeat_enable (noise_check C).
B28.visual_intent: Code card at left: the same scroll shader with the hint removed from the uniform line; at right the real render: the clouds drift for a moment, then the right side of the disc smears into horizontal streaks that grow leftward as time passes. A terracotta ring on the streaks.
B28.motion_claim: Streaks grow from the right edge and take over the picture while the clouds stop moving there.

show.event: the uniform line without its hint
ring on the streaks; they have spread

B28.why: A real streak growing across the picture is the failure the hint prevents; a drawing would not show how it spreads.

cues.label: repeat_enable: past one, wrap to the start

B29.capture_spec: C14: scene script: NoiseTexture2D with FastNoiseLite defaults, 512 x 512, seamless OFF, bound to lab-shaders/11-noise-scroll.gdshader on the square target; 12 s, 30 fps, Forward+, `--time-origin 0` (the seam then sits at UV x 0.9 at 1 s and 0.2 at 8 s). Verified: the plain texture's wrap difference is 14.25x the normal neighbour difference; the render's biggest column jump sits at the wrap position (ratio 7.4 to 7.7) and moves as 1 - 0.1 * TIME (77 px per 3 s step).
B29.visual_intent: Code card at left (the hint is back on the uniform line); at right the real render with a plain, non-seamless noise texture: the clouds scroll forever, and a straight vertical line, a seam, crosses the disc and travels left. A terracotta ring on the seam.
B29.motion_claim: The seam travels left across the disc as the clouds scroll.

show.event: clouds wrap; the seam enters the disc

B29.why: A straight line cutting through the clouds is the defect; only a real render shows how visible it is.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · two NoiseTexture2D, seamless off and on
props.caption: seamless: the edges match, so repeats show no seam

B30.capture_spec: C15: two-panel scene script (`--scene`): two square targets side by side with lab-shaders/11-noise-scroll.gdshader, left NoiseTexture2D seamless off, right seamless on (same FastNoiseLite defaults, 512 x 512); 12 s, 30 fps, Forward+, `--time-origin 0`. Verified: wrap difference 14.25x the neighbour difference (off) against 1.07x (on); contrast (standard deviation) 0.168 against 0.158; the render has no outlier column with seamless on (ratio 1.3 to 1.6).
B30.visual_intent: Two real Godot panels side by side showing the scrolling disc: the left uses a plain noise texture and a seam crosses it; the right uses the same settings with Seamless switched on and no seam appears. Labels 'seamless off' and 'seamless on'.
B30.motion_claim: The seam crosses the left disc while the right disc scrolls cleanly.
B30.why: The two results under the same scroll are the proof; the seam is a motion across the picture.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · progress swept by script

B31.capture_spec: C16: custom scene as C11 (seamless on) with lab-shaders/13-noise-reveal.gdshader, progress held 0 for 1 s, swept to 1 by 9 s, held (`--animate progress:0:0,1:0,9:1`); 12 s, 30 fps, Forward+. Verified: coverage of the disc interior 1.3 % / 43.7 % / 93.1 % at progress 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 (noise_check R).
B31.visual_intent: Code card at left (the reveal shader); at right the real render: as progress climbs from 0 to 1 the disc blooms in blotches, small islands first, then merging until the whole disc is on. A label with the progress value.
B31.motion_claim: Islands of teal appear, grow and merge as the number climbs.
B31.why: The reveal is a motion by nature; the real render shows the noise's own blotch pattern.

B32.visual_intent: Top: a bell-shaped histogram of the noise values from 0 to 1 (20 bars, real data from noise_check T-seamless), centred near 0.5. Below it the cumulative curve from the same noise (real data, noise_check R-curve): an S rising slowly, then fast, then slowly. Three terracotta dots on the curve at progress 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, labelled '1 %', '44 %' and '93 %'. Label 'progress is not percent shown' and the small grey credit 'Apple M4 Pro · Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · NoiseTexture2D defaults'.
B32.motion_claim: The bars rise into a bell, the curve draws as their running total, and the three dots land at 1, 44 and 93 percent.
B32.why: A running total of a bell is an S-curve: the same shape as smoothstep, and the picture shows why the pace is uneven.
